pages.claim: Can caesium incorporation remove the damp-heat failure route of a mixed-halide absorber?

notes.say: Frame the question, not the paper. The room knows phase segregation, so the opening has to define what a satisfactory answer would look like: a retention number, a mechanism-side measurement, and an explicit statement of what is still unknown.
notes.checkpoint: Question on screen before the first data slide

pages.claim: 1000 h of damp heat separates the two absorbers: 73.8 % retention for the reference, 96.2 % with Cs
bullets: Same cycling conditions for both groups

notes.say: Lead with the contrast. Both groups started at nearly the same efficiency, so the entire gap at 1000 h is a difference in degradation rate, not in the starting point. Do not explain the mechanism yet; let the number sit for a moment before moving on.
notes.checkpoint: Audience has seen the retention contrast

pages.claim: The Cs-incorporated absorber trades a little initial efficiency for damp-heat stability
bullets: Reference: 21.4 % at the start, 15.8 % after 1000 h
Cs-incorporated: 20.9 % at the start, 20.1 % after 1000 h
The gap opens over time, not at the start

notes.say: Quantify the trade. The reference loses about a quarter of its efficiency; the Cs-incorporated film loses almost nothing. Say explicitly that this is an encapsulated device result under lab cycling and that nothing here is a module-level claim.
notes.checkpoint: Trade-off stated as a rate difference

pages.claim: What moves with retention is the delta-phase fraction, not the starting efficiency
bullets: Reference film: 31.5 % delta phase at the end

notes.say: This is the part of the story that was not settled before: the amount of photo-inactive delta phase tracks how much efficiency survives. When asked why phase fraction should be the read-out, point at the ordering rather than at the absolute values.

notes.say: Keep this short and concrete: the room cares about the encapsulation stack and the sampling density, not about the spin-coating recipe. Mention that the same encapsulation and the same chamber were used for both groups, which is what makes the comparison meaningful.
notes.checkpoint: Protocol and sample size on screen

notes.say: Say the limit before anyone asks for it. The honest sentence is that this shows a rate difference inside one stack, and that an extrapolated lifetime would need a longer window and more temperatures. Then stop talking.
notes.checkpoint: A limitation is stated by us, not extracted from us

pages.claim: Cs incorporation keeps the black phase and retains 96.2 % of initial PCE after 1000 h
bullets: T80 extended from 240 h to 1450 h
Open item: outdoor validation, not covered here

notes.say: Close on the one sentence the room should remember, then hand over the open item. Do not re-read the agenda or re-list the slides; the conclusion is stronger when it is said once.

qa.question: Is the comparison fair, given that the Cs-incorporated group starts at a lower efficiency?
qa.answer: Yes for the point being made: both groups start between 20.9 % and 21.4 %, and the 1000 h endpoint is 20.1 % versus 15.8 %, so the difference is in the degradation rate rather than in the starting point. A starting-efficiency-matched control is not shown in this excerpt, and that is worth saying out loud.

qa.question: Which measurement actually supports the stability claim: efficiency or phase fraction?
qa.answer: Both, and they agree. The phase fraction is the mechanism-side read-out (31.5 % vs 4.2 % delta phase) and retention is the device-side read-out (73.8 % vs 96.2 %). Presenting them together is what makes the claim more than a single-number result.

qa.question: Can a three-temperature Arrhenius fit really support a 1.12 eV activation energy?
qa.answer: Only weakly. Three temperatures is the minimum for a straight-line fit and no error bars are given, so 1.12 eV should be presented as an estimate. If pressed, say the fix is a temperature series with repeats rather than a re-fit of the same data.

qa.question: How long would the Cs-incorporated absorber last outdoors?
qa.answer: Not answered by this work. The window is 1000 h of lab damp-heat cycling on one encapsulation stack, with no outdoor or module-scale data. Any outdoor lifetime figure would be an extrapolation outside the study, so decline to give one.
